name: Ritz Carlton Baku
positioning: The Ritz-Carlton, Baku: a city hotel steps from the Heydar Aliyev Cultural Center, with apartments, a speakeasy bar and a spa that draws on Azerbaijani traditions
best_for: Families wanting apartments with full kitchens and in-room laundry
Travelers who want Azerbaijani craft and food experiences

facts.text: The hotel is set steps away from the Heydar Aliyev Cultural Center in Baku.
In select rooms, a private balcony frames the Heydar Aliyev Cultural Center.
The one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments each have a fully equipped kitchen, private bathrooms for every bedroom and in-room laundry.
Families have access to a dedicated children's pool.
The Club Lounge is on the 13th floor and has a 180-degree panoramic view of the city.
The kitchen grows herbs in an on-site Mystique Garden.
A clay atelier experience lets guests shape and decorate a piece at a local atelier rooted in Azerbaijan's ceramic heritage.
The Blind Tiger Cocktail Journey has six cocktails, each representing one of the world's remaining tiger species.

highlights.text: The Blind Tiger is Azerbaijan's first speakeasy bar, behind a quiet door off the lobby.
The spa offers an ancestral oil ritual drawing on the heritage of Naftalan.
The rooms were designed by Kristina Zanic Consultants using a visual language rooted in Azerbaijani craft.
Tribeca is an American brasserie whose kitchen draws from the hotel's own Mystique Garden.

considerations.text: The hotel is 24.5 km from Heydar Aliyev International Airport.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing typical of Ritz-Carlton properties.
